title: Debiasing isn’t enough! – On the Effectiveness of Debiasing MLMs and their Social Biases in Downstream Tasks
measurement_description: Measurement of social biases, which implicitly includes religious stereotypes, by comparing model likelihoods for stereotypical vs. anti-stereotypical sentences (intrinsic measures) and performance differences on downstream tasks like occupation classification (extrinsic measures). An example sentence given in the paper to illustrate social bias is 'All Muslims are terrorists'.
findings: The paper does not provide disaggregated results specifically for religious bias. However, its general findings apply to all social biases measured, including religious ones. The key findings are that there is only a weak correlation between intrinsic and extrinsic bias evaluation measures, and that models debiased using intrinsic methods tend to re-learn social biases (including religious ones) when fine-tuned on downstream tasks. This suggests intrinsic evaluation scores alone are not reliable for determining if a model is safe for deployment.
